extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of poetry, literature, and art criticism; poets and critics studying Greek literature and aesthetic theory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging or producing poetry and fine art with emphasis on Greek literature: focuses on poetic truth, universality, restraint, unity, plausibility, and the relation of poetry to history and philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic truth (construction according to laws of poetic truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be constructed according to the laws of poetic truth so that even impossible adventures and fantastic elements are presented in a way that makes the fiction 'look like truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irrational elements may appear but must be accessories that do not disturb the main impression; present the impossible to the imagination 'with such vividness and coherence that the impossible becomes plausible.' Example: The Odyssey's magic elements are coherent within the poem's imaginative logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful representation of human life and action
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole should be a faithful representation of human life and action; imagination should not override believable human behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when including supernatural or fantastical elements, the central depiction of human motives and actions must remain convincing and central to the work's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence and vividness of imaginative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fantastic or impossible elements must be presented vividly and coherently so they do not break the reader's sense of plausibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vivid description and internal coherence are required to assimilate the extraordinary into the poem's truth; lack of coherence makes the irrational jarring rather than poetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint, measure, and self-restraint of imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet's imagination should be under the control of reason, limited by a sense of measure and a faculty of self-restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gratuitous dazzling or prodigal excess; the artist may 'do much more if he chose, but he does not care to dazzle us.' Reserve and temperate strength enhance the work's dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials fused according to what is possible and natural
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaginative materials should be fused and combined 'according to the laws of what is possible, reasonable, natural.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition should respect plausibility and internal necessity; selection and combination of elements should avoid hybrid compounds that contradict natural intelligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of non-essential attributes (economy of characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes that are non-essential to a figure's function or meaning should be eliminated so characters and gods stand out clear and unified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In myth-making and character-assignment, discard accreted or redundant traits to avoid unmeaning chaos and to create clear, enduring types (e.g., Homeric gods with redistributed, coherent functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality — aim at the permanent and essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry should aim at the universal: it represents the permanent possibilities of human nature, the essentials rather than the accidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet tells 'what may happen according to laws of internal probability or necessity' rather than merely recording empirical events; universality gives lasting significance and philosophical weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical or conceivable sequence over empirical sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence in poetry should be the logical or conceivable sequence of ideas (intrinsic probability/necessity), not merely the empirical sequence of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic causality should reveal unity and meaning; eliminate chance where it undermines the poem's internal logic and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typicality and simplification of character to reveal universals
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters (especially in Greek poetry) should be drawn as elemental, typical figures (maiden, wife, mother, etc.) so their behaviour expresses general human truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifying accidental or superficial traits can deepen individuality and make characters exemplary; maintain sufficient subtlety of detail insofar as it contributes to the total impression and unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit variety of detail only when it serves total unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine shades of character and variety of detail are admitted only when they contribute to the total impression and are subject to a controlling unity of design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow particulars that enrich the central type, but excise material that distracts from the controlling artistic unity (example: Antigone retains subtle traits without losing typal force).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetical inspiration must remain subject to reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if poetry is 'a thing inspired' or compared to madness, the poet's inspiration must not abandon the sovereignty of reason; imaginative creations obey a hidden law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspiration (ecstasy, frenzy) is compatible with artistic control; caprice and inconsequence are signs of failure, whereas the 'true poet dreams being awake' and subjugates fancy to consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy's licence must have an underlying method
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy may revel in absurdity and overturn the world, but even its wildest licence should contain some underlying reason, intelligible drift, and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid transitions and seemingly inconsequent jokes are acceptable within comedy, provided they fit an internal method and contribute to the work's effect rather than producing mere incoherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as concrete philosophy (expressing universals in sensuous form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is akin to philosophy insofar as it aims at the universal, but distinct because it employs sensuous and imaginative form; it is 'a concrete philosophy' or 'a criticism of life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High imaginative works embody an interpretation of man and life—a latent connected scheme—without systematising it explicitly; the poem's form should carry its philosophical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fusion of poetry and history — myth as preserved collective truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Myth and poetic narrative may function as authentic history in a poetic, idealising sense, preserving collective memory and the substantial truth of the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry can project present realities into an idealised past, using myth to give historical perspective and to transfigure individuals into symbols of their race or community (Pindaric ode example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Idealisation is fulfilment, not opposition, of the real
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal in art should be the fulfilment and perfection of reality, not its negation; ideal and real spring from the same soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not set up the ideal as merely abstract or opposite to the real; aim to perfect and complete real experience through artistic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extravagant and grotesque symbolic hybrids
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid producing hybrid compounds of symbolic attributes or grotesque extravagance (ascribed here to Oriental art) that lack counterpart in the world of reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols should remain intelligible and harmonious; use symbolic representation that appeals to the imagination without devolving into incoherent monster-like hybrids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic probability and moral plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Events and actions in poetry should conform to internal moral probability — 'what may happen' — rather than improbable or arbitrary occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral improbabilities that break character or internal logic should be excluded; the poet should ensure that character actions follow from established motives and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fancy in non-comic genres should be restrained and transient
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside comedy, fancy should appear as restrained, transient gleams that do not disturb the serenity of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let imaginative flights be sudden illuminations that enrich rather than overwhelm the poem's controlling reason and unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevating the particular to the universal (e.g., odes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poems (such as odes) should rise from the individual occasion to a larger, universal meaning by connecting the particular to mythic or historical perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the particular event or person as an entry point to broader themes—'the victor is transfigured into a glorious personification of his race'—so the work attains panhellenic or universal resonance.
